blocks.text: Dear Ms. Sutton:

Thank you for the confidence you have placed in us over the past few days. This letter confirms the terms on which our firm will support {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} through the current matter, and it should be read alongside the conversation we had when you first called. If any part of it sits differently from what we discussed, tell me and we will set it right before either of us signs.
The Work Before Us

Our task is to help {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} respond to the present situation clearly, quickly, and with a single voice, and then to steady the firm's standing once the immediate pressure has eased. We treat a matter like this for what it is, a communications problem laid over a real set of facts, and we will not let the message run ahead of what you can stand behind.

The audiences that matter here are distinct rather than many: your clients and referral sources, your own people, the press that follows the firm, and the wider professional community whose regard the firm depends on. Each will read the same facts a little differently, and part of our job is to see that the firm speaks to each in a way that is true, consistent, and mindful of the others listening in.

In practice, that means preparing the holding language and the fuller statements you may need at short notice, deciding who should say what to which audience and in what order, and keeping a close watch on how the matter is being reported and discussed. It also means readying the people who will speak for the firm, so that when a hard question comes they answer it the same way and without surprise.

Our method is deliberately calm. We begin by getting the facts straight with you and your counsel, we agree the small number of things the firm most needs understood, and we build every message back to those. We will also settle a simple approval path at the outset, so that in a fast-moving hour it is clear who can clear a statement and who must be told; speed matters in a crisis, and the path is there so that quick does not become careless.
The People You Will Work With

I will keep this account in my own hands and be your point of contact for anything sensitive or urgent while the matter is active. On the statements that carry the most weight, nothing will go out without my sign-off.

Amy Carter will run the work day to day, holding the thread together, turning our conversations into drafts, and making sure a promised follow-up actually reaches you. She is steady under a tight clock and easy to reach.

Nancy Suarez will keep the moving parts in order, shepherding approvals, tracking the timeline, and seeing that every version is logged and current. Between the two of them, you will always know where a piece of work stands.
Fees and Payment

Our fee for the engagement is {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}, covering the work described above and the counsel of the team through the period. We have set it as a fixed fee so that you can call on us as the matter demands without watching a clock.

The fee covers our people and their time. It does not cover out-of-pocket costs such as travel, media monitoring taken in your name, or third-party services you ask us to arrange; those we pass through at cost and only with your agreement in advance. We invoice monthly, payable within thirty days.
Commencement and Term

The engagement begins {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}} and is expected to run about eight months, which reflects both the active phase of the matter and the quieter work of rebuilding afterward. If the situation resolves sooner, we will say so and wind the work down rather than fill the time.

Either of us may end the engagement on fourteen days' written notice. If you bring it to a close, you owe us for the work done and the costs committed to that point, and we will hand over our files and working materials so that nothing is left stranded.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}, the matter, and the people involved we will hold in strict confidence and use only for the purpose of this engagement. Given the nature of the work, we will also be careful with our own internal handling, keeping the account on a need-to-know footing within the firm.
Limitation of Liability

We will do this work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect from an experienced adviser, and we stand behind it. We are advisers on communications, though, not on the law or on the underlying facts, and our liability to you under this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it. We do not warrant any particular outcome in the press, in the market, or before any other audience.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute under it will be resolved there. Nothing in it displaces the duty we owe you as your communications adviser.
If this reflects our understanding, please sign below and return one copy to me, keeping the other for your records. Once it is back, Amy Carter will send the kickoff note and we will begin.

To: The {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} engagement team
From: Amy Carter
Re: Getting the crisis communications work under way

We are under way on the crisis communications work for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}, which began {{fact:f:E-2021-001.start}}, and I want us all working from the same picture before the pace picks up. Our aim for the firm is easy to state and harder to do: help them respond to the current matter with one clear voice, protect their standing with the people whose regard they rely on, and leave them steadier than we found them.

A word on how we run an account like this. We keep it small, we write things down early, and we over-share among ourselves so that two people never end up guessing at the same question. The client is under real strain, so our own side needs to be calm and orderly enough that they never feel it in ours.
How we will split the work

items: Message and materials. I hold the drafting: the holding language, the fuller statements, and the question-and-answer set the firm needs ready to hand. Everything traces back to the small set of points we agree with Julie and the client.
Approvals and sequence. Nancy Suarez owns the approval path and the running order, so we always know who has cleared a statement and which audience hears it first.
Monitoring. We keep a daily read on coverage and reaction and flag anything that needs a same-day response, rather than being caught out by it.
Client coordination. Megan Sutton is our single point of contact on their side; requests and approvals route through her so nothing gets lost across two firms.
Spokesperson readiness. Ahead of any interview or briefing, we prepare whoever is speaking so the answers are consistent and rehearsed.

blocks.text: The first moves

items: Nancy Suarez confirms the approval path with Megan Sutton and circulates it to all of us by the end of the week.
I draft the initial holding statement and a first cut of the question-and-answer set for Julie's review.
We stand up the monitoring and agree a short daily check-in for as long as the matter is live.
Megan Sutton gathers the internal contacts and any statements the firm has already made, so we are not starting cold.

blocks.text: The piece that has to land first is the approval path, because nearly everything else keys off knowing who can clear a statement in a hurry. Nancy Suarez will have it in front of Megan Sutton tomorrow, and once it is agreed we move on the holding language. Flag anything here that looks off before then.
Megan,

I am starting this thread so our updates on the current matter stay in one place and are easy to find later. For the record, the working contacts are set: Megan Sutton on your side, and on ours Nancy Suarez, copied here, who keeps our approvals and timeline in order alongside me. Each note we send will tie back to the piece of work it concerns, so the thread stays easy to follow.

We have made a steady start. The holding language is agreed and in your hands, and we are now building out the fuller statement and a short question-and-answer set for the people at {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} who may be asked directly. You should have a first draft of both from us early next week. Nothing has gone out beyond the holding language, and nothing will without your sign-off.

Two things would help before that draft firms up. A read from you on which audience the firm most wants to reach first would let us sequence it well, and it would help to know who besides you should be cleared to speak if a question lands while you are away from your desk. A short call works if that is easier than writing it out.
Regards

blocks.text: Matters discussed

The team met by video to review progress at the midpoint of the engagement. Nancy Suarez chaired and kept these minutes. The purpose was to check the active response against plan and to set the next round of work.

Amy Carter reported that the holding statement and the core question-and-answer set are in use and holding up. Two press queries have come in since the last session. Both were answered from the approved lines without escalation.

The fuller statement is drafted and cleared but has not been needed. It stays on file, ready to release if the matter widens. Amy Carter noted the question-and-answer set has been updated twice as new questions surfaced.

The group reviewed coverage to date. Reporting has been factual and has not widened beyond the original matter. Megan Sutton confirmed that internal questions at {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} have slowed, which the group read as a sign the first phase is settling.
The approval path was reviewed. Every statement this period cleared through Nancy Suarez to Megan Sutton, and turnaround stayed under an hour when it was needed. No change to the path was proposed.

Discussion turned to the next phase. With the immediate response steady, the work shifts toward the firm's standing over the coming months. Amy Carter will draft a short plan for proactive contact with key clients and referral sources, for partner sign-off before anything goes out.

Megan Sutton raised employee communications. Staff had the initial notice but nothing since. The group agreed a brief follow-up to employees is due and set an owner for it. It goes out within the week, once the wording is cleared.

Amy Carter asked whether the firm should say anything proactively while the matter is quiet. The group decided to hold for now and revisit at the next session; the outreach plan should be ready before the firm speaks unprompted.
On cadence, the daily check-in will step down to twice weekly while the matter is quiet. It returns to daily if anything breaks.
Actions

rows: Draft a proactive outreach plan for key clients and referral sources
Prepare a short follow-up note to employees for the client's review
Confirm the revised twice-weekly check-in with the team
Gather an up-to-date contact list for priority clients

Status Report: Crisis Communications for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}

rows: Amy Carter, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: Where the engagement stands

We have reached the midpoint of the crisis communications work for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}, and I am glad to report the engagement is on plan and, in a couple of places, a little ahead of it. The first half was about response: getting in front of the matter with clear, consistent language and making sure the firm spoke with one voice under pressure. That footing is now steady, and the work is beginning to turn from holding the line to rebuilding the firm's standing.

What follows sets out what this period produced, what comes next, where the budget sits, and the risks I am watching. None of it changes the direction we set at the outset; it carries that direction into the quieter months ahead.
What we accomplished this period

Most of the effort went into standing up a response the firm could rely on without hesitation. We agreed the small set of points that matter most, built the holding statement and a fuller question-and-answer set around them, and put both into use as queries came in. Nancy Suarez set up the approval path early, so every statement has cleared the same route and nothing has gone out unreviewed.

Alongside the drafting, we prepared the handful of people most likely to be asked about the matter, walking them through the lines until the answers came back consistent. The daily monitoring has done its job as well: the coverage has stayed factual and narrow, and where a question looked likely to escalate we had a same-day response ready before it did.

items: An agreed message architecture: a short core statement and the supporting lines that answer the questions the firm is most likely to face.
A holding statement and a working question-and-answer set, both in use and revised as the matter has developed.
A daily monitoring read on coverage and reaction, with a same-day flag for anything needing a response.
A clear approval path, owned by Nancy Suarez, so statements clear quickly and consistently.

blocks.text: The work ahead

With the immediate response steady, the second half turns to the firm's standing over the coming months. We move from reacting to reaching out: a measured program of contact with the clients and referral sources whose regard matters most, refreshed language for the firm's own channels, and a short internal update so staff hear from leadership rather than from rumor. None of this reopens the response; it builds on the footing we have set.

The order matters more than the pace. Reaching a handful of the most important relationships properly does more for the firm than a wide, generic note that reads as reputation management. Nancy Suarez and I will draft the plan around the names you give us and bring it to you before any of it goes out.

items: A proactive outreach plan for priority clients and referral sources, for the partner's sign-off before anything goes out.
Refreshed boilerplate and website language that reflects where the firm now stands.
A follow-up note to employees, kept plain and honest.
A short readiness refresh for spokespeople ahead of the quieter phase.

blocks.text: The budget

The engagement is tracking within its fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2021-001.fee}}, and the first half came in on the effort we scoped. The round-the-clock stretch of the response is behind us, which should keep the second half comfortably inside the fee. If something outside the original plan comes up, such as a fresh development that needs a full new statement, I will flag it and agree it with you before we take it on.
Risks I am watching
Three things are worth naming now, while each is still easy to manage. None threatens the engagement, and each has a plan sitting against it.

items: A second development. A crisis can be reopened by a new fact or a new inquiry. We keep the holding lines current and the approval path warm so we are not caught flat if that happens.
Consistency of voice. Several people at the firm may be asked about the matter. The question-and-answer set and a short spokesperson refresh are there to keep everyone answering the same way.
Timing of the outreach. The outreach only lands if the moment is right, and we will judge that with you rather than fix it in advance by the calendar.

blocks.text: The one thing I need from you before the next period is a short list of the clients and referral sources you would want us to reach first, which lets us shape the outreach plan around the relationships that matter most to you. I will send a note to set a time to walk through it, and Nancy Suarez and I will have a first draft ready for that conversation.

Present

Amy Carter, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: Matters discussed

The team met by video to review the engagement in its later stage and to plan for close-out. Nancy Suarez chaired and recorded these minutes. The matter is quiet, and the discussion focused on the wind-down and handover.

Amy Carter reported that the proactive outreach is largely complete. The priority clients and referral sources have been contacted, the responses have been steady, and there is no sign the matter has cost the firm a core relationship.
Two clients had asked direct questions during the outreach. Both were answered from the standing lines, and neither has raised the matter since. Amy Carter judged the relationships intact.

Coverage has stopped. There has been no new reporting in several weeks, and monitoring is down to a weekly scan. The group agreed monitoring can end at close-out, with a note to the firm on how to watch for any late resurfacing on its own.
Megan Sutton confirmed that internal sentiment at {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}} has recovered. The employee follow-up landed well, and there are no open questions from staff.

Nancy Suarez reported that the firm's website language and standard boilerplate still carry the crisis-period phrasing. The group agreed both should return to normal wording as part of close-out, so nothing keeps signalling an active matter once this one has passed.

The group turned to close-out. The remaining work is to refresh the firm's standard language for normal use, assemble a short handover pack, and hold a final review with leadership. Amy Carter will draft the handover; Nancy Suarez will assemble the file of statements and approvals for the client's records.
Nancy Suarez confirmed the file is nearly complete. Every statement, its approver, and the date it cleared is logged, and the only remaining gap is the last stretch of monitoring notes.

Megan Sutton asked whether the firm should keep any capability on standby after the engagement ends. The group agreed to include a brief section in the handover on what to do if the matter resurfaces, setting out who to call and the first steps, so the firm is not starting cold.

Amy Carter suggested a short closing note to the priority contacts who engaged during the outreach. The group agreed a brief, warm thank-you is worth sending as part of close-out, kept free of any reference to the matter itself.
Actions

rows: Draft the close-out handover pack, including a section on what to do if the matter resurfaces
Assemble the file of statements and approvals for the client
Refresh the firm's standard boilerplate for normal use
Schedule the final review with leadership
